title: Sri Lanka Easter attacks convicts to challenge 200-year jail terms
byline: Fifteen people convicted over Sri Lanka’s 2019 Easter Sunday suicide attacks will challenge their jail terms of more than 200 years each, a defence lawyer said on Wednesday. The attacks, carried out by nine suicide bombers from the local Islamist extremist group National Thawheed Jamaat, linked to ISIS, had targeted three Catholic churches and three luxury hotels on April 21, 2019.

title: One dead, two injured in Moratuwa Soysapura Housing Complex fire
byline: One person was killed and two others sustained injuries following a sudden fire that broke out in Block ’C’ of the Soysapura Housing Complex in Moratuwa tonight (23).

title: Habib Rifan sworn in as MP
byline: Habib Rifan was sworn in as a National List Member of Parliament representing the Sri Lanka Muslim Congress (SLMC) before Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne today.

title: Opposition holds protest near Parliamentary Complex
byline: The Opposition is currently holding a protest at Polduwa Junction near the Parliamentary Complex.

title: Revenue license system goes offline in eight provinces for four days
byline: The electronic Revenue License (eRL 2.0) system will be temporarily suspended in eight provinces from Friday, September 25, to Monday, September 28, 2026, due to a scheduled system upgrade.

title: Galle Face child abuse case: Police seek information to identify suspect
byline: Sri Lanka Police have launched an investigation to identify and apprehend a suspect allegedly involved in the abduction and sexual abuse of a 13-year-old girl at Galle Face Green in Colombo.

title: Trump offers warm welcome as China’s Xi arrives for US visit
byline: US President Donald Trump has greeted his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping with a military flyover and 100ft (30m) red carpet to kick off their three-day summit in Washington.

title: Flood warning for Kuda Ganga extended by 48 hours
byline: The Irrigation Department has extended the flood warning issued for the Kuda Ganga sub-basin of the Kalu River for a further 48 hours.

title: Police uncover real story behind viral ‘extortion’ video
byline: Pettah Police have launched an investigation into a video circulating on social media that was widely shared as an alleged extortion incident in the Maradana-Panchikawatta area.

title: Judges will have option of retiring early despite new retirement age: Minister
byline: Judges will have the option of retiring early with their full pensions despite the new retirement age, Minister of Justice Harshana Nanayakkara told Parliament today.

title: No regrets whatsoever, accused still hold onto their ideology: ASG
byline: Delivering the judgment, High Court Judge Navaratne Marasinghe observed that a conspiracy does not require all those involved to be physically present together or to have directly communicated with one another.

title: What is the 22nd Amendment to the Constitution?
byline: The much-awaited Twenty-Second Amendment to the Constitution is set to be debated in Parliament this week, with the second reading of the Bill scheduled to continue on Friday (25), following the Supreme Court’s determination that the proposed amendment does not require approval at a referendum.

title: Bill on dog registration and rabies elimination presented in Parliament
byline: A Bill titled the “Elimination of Rabies and Registration of Dogs” was presented to Parliament today by the Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government.

title: Parliamentary debate on 22nd Amendment begins
byline: The two-day parliamentary debate on the proposed 22nd Amendment to the Constitution commenced a short while ago.

title: Security tightened around Parliament amid 22nd Amendment debate
byline: Security has been tightened in and around the Parliamentary complex as Parliament debates the 22nd Amendment to the Constitution today.

title: Australia says OpenAI agent hacked into government website
byline: Australia said on Wednesday (Sep 23) an OpenAI agent breached a government health data portal in June, gaining unauthorised access to files, in what could be the first known instance of an AI agent hacking a government website.

title: Common standards for preschools targeted for 2027
byline: Plans to introduce common standards for all preschools by 2027 were discussed at the Ministerial Consultative Committee on Women and Child Affairs.

title: Legal amendments to ban corporal punishment of children discussed
byline: Legal amendments required to prohibit corporal punishment of children were discussed at the Ministerial Consultative Committee on Women and Child Affairs.

title: New mandatory training for first-time Japan, Romania job seekers
byline: The Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment (SLBFE) has introduced mandatory pre-migration training for first-time job seekers travelling to Japan and Romania.

title: Ministry pledges support for wildlife officers facing baseless allegations
byline: The Ministry of Environment has assured that it will provide legal and administrative support to wildlife and veterinary officers who face false or baseless allegations while properly performing their duties.

title: Urgent treatment begins for ‘Kavantissa’ elephant in Galgamuwa
byline: Urgent veterinary treatment has commenced for ‘Kavantissa’, the elephant roaming in the Galgamuwa area, following an operation carried out by a special team of the Department of Wildlife Conservation this morning.

title: NPP unity will be clear in 22nd Amendment vote: Harini
byline: Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya said the unity of the National People’s Power (NPP) parliamentary group would be clearly demonstrated during tomorrow evening’s vote on the 22nd Amendment.

title: Former Krrish Group Director Janaki Siriwardena arrested
byline: Former Krrish Group Director Janaki Siriwardena has been arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC).

title: Judge temporarily overturns Trump’s White House media ban
byline: A judge has ordered the Trump administration to immediately reinstate access to the White House for three news organisations barred from the building last week by the president.

title: Piumi Hansamali withdraws writ petition challenging CID probe
byline: Sri Lankan model, actress and beauty entrepreneur Piumi Hansamali today withdrew her writ petition filed before the Court of Appeal challenging the legality of investigations conducted by the CID’s Illegal Assets Investigations Division into the alleged suspicious acquisition of property.

title: Transport medical tokens go online today
byline: A free online token system for obtaining Transport Medical Certificates will be introduced today (24), the National Institute of Transport Medicine said.

title: Dambulla tourist hotel fined Rs. 500,000 for overcharging on bottled water
byline: A tourist hotel in Dambulla was fined Rs. 500,000 after being found guilty of selling a bottle of drinking water marked at Rs. 100 for Rs. 300, the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) said.

title: Harry Potter play producer says cost of living made two-part show ’impossible’
byline: A Harry Potter And The Cursed Child producer has said the rising cost of living made it ’’literally impossible’’ to retain the play’s original format in two parts.

title: Sri Lanka, UAE discuss Trincomalee regional energy hub
byline: Sri Lanka and the United Arab Emirates have discussed the ongoing UAE-India-Sri Lanka tripartite initiative to develop Trincomalee as a regional energy hub, during a meeting between UAE Ambassador to Sri Lanka Khaled Nasser Al Ameri and Deputy Speaker of Parliament Dr. Rizvie Salih.

title: Justice must be accessible to all without discrimination: PM
byline: Justice must be accessible to all without discrimination, while establishing the rule of law and ensuring equal access to justice remain among the Government’s key commitments, Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya said today.

title: CSE slips as foreign selling weighs on recent recovery
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange closed marginally lower on 24 September 2026, with both benchmark indices reversing early gains as selling pressure returned during the session.

title: National media guidelines proposed to protect children’s privacy
byline: National Media Guidelines have been prepared to protect the dignity, privacy and confidentiality of children when reporting news involving them, the Ministerial Consultative Committee on Women and Child Affairs was informed.

title: Vijitha Herath to address UN General Assembly on September 28
byline: Sri Lanka’s Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism Minister Vijitha Herath is scheduled to travel to New York on September 26 to represent Sri Lanka at the 81st United Nations General Assembly and deliver the country’s national statement on September 28.

title: Ruling party MPs pose for photo in Parliament canteen
byline: A group of ruling party MPs posed for a photograph with Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) MP Namal Rajapaksa at the members’ canteen of Parliament today.

title: Technical committee to decide on mothers with children under five leaving for foreign jobs
byline: A final decision on the issue of mothers with children below five years leaving the country for foreign employment will be taken by a technical committee, the Ministerial Consultative Committee on Women and Child Affairs was informed.

title: Diplomats, UN and civil society assess Sri Lanka’s SDG progress
byline: Sri Lanka’s progress and challenges in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by 2030 came under discussion today as diplomats, UN officials and civil society representatives called for continued efforts to advance the country’s SDG agenda.

title: SLBFE warns Israel job seekers over fake recruitment link
byline: The Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment has warned job seekers to be cautious of a fraudulent online recruitment link circulating on social media in connection with alleged free employment opportunities in Israel.

title: Heavy rain up to 100mm forecast for next 36 hours
byline: Heavy showers of up to around 100 mm, strong winds and thunderstorms are expected in several parts of the country during the next 36 hours, the Meteorological Department warned today (24).

title: Former Krrish director Janaki Siriwardena remanded
byline: Former Krrish Group director Janaki Siriwardena, who was arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) over an alleged Rs. 70 million bribe paid to Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa, was ordered to be remanded until October 6 by Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama.

title: Fake website misuses Foreign Bureau name to collect job seekers’ personal data
byline: The Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment (SLBFE) has warned the public about a fake website that is illegally using the Bureau’s name, official logo and photographs to collect personal information from people seeking employment opportunities in Israel.
